_README: MANUALLY CURATED from official Rutgers catalog prose (Phase 7.3, 2026-10-23), the
B.S. option of the same Computer Science major page as sas-198-ba.json. Requirements
1 and 2 are the B.A.'s, copied node for node; category 3 asks SEVEN electives; the
science requirement is encoded as one choice among the sets the prose lists.
Prompt 08 B1 (2026-11-11): the elective list and its constraints are now SOURCED from the
archived department pages (B.S. degree page and electives page, raw HTML captured
2026-11-09, sha256 in data/programs/rutgers/sources.json) instead of an unarchived note.
The B.S. page's own wording settles the 300-level question; the 493/494 cap is modeled
(group_caps). Two source disagreements stay OPEN and visible: CS-INTRO-2027 (121/122 vs
111/112) and CS-BS-COPY (B.S. page clauses labelled 'B.A.'). PENDING human review.
review_questions: CS-INTRO-2027: the department requires 01:198:121/122 from Spring 2027 while the catalog names 111/112 (and 111 is not offered in Spring 2027). Which governs students on the 2026-2027 catalog, and is 121/122 an equivalent of 111/112?
CS-BS-COPY: do the residency (seven 01:198 courses) and ten-year elective clauses on the B.S. page bind B.S. students? The page labels them 'B.A.'.
The physics list names '01:750:193 and 194' twice ('... or 01:750:193 and 194 ... or 01:750:193, 194'). Encoded once. Confirm no other course was meant.
Chemistry 01:160:171 appears in all three chemistry options; each option is encoded as its own all-of set.
Same graduate-course question as the B.A. (sas-198-ba.json review_questions).

program_version.source_prose: The B.A. option requires 51-55 credits (depending on 3-credit or 4-credit elective options); the B.S. option requires 67-72 credits.

requirements.name: Computer Science B.S. Major
requirements.source_prose: The basic major, leading to a bachelor of arts (B.A.) degree, consists of: 1) six required courses in computer science, 01:198:111, 112, 205, 206, 211, and 344; 2) three courses in mathematics, 01:640:151-152 and 01:640:250; and 3) five electives from a designated list of courses in computer science and related disciplines.

requirements.name: Data Structures

requirements.name: Design and Analysis of Computer Algorithms
Computer Science Electives
requirements.notes: The designated list is the Department of Computer Science electives page (archived capture phase08a-cs-electives, raw HTML, 2026-11-09), to which the catalog defers: 30 CS courses plus Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, Philosophy, Linguistics and Statistics options - identical to the list encoded 2026-10-23. Constraints from the department B.S. page: at least five of the seven in 01:198 (encoded as at most two outside subject 198; every listed course outside 198 is also outside unit 01:198), at least two of those at the 300 level or above, and at most one 01:198:493/494 (group cap).
requirements.source_prose: complete seven courses from category 3, no more than two of these outside the Department of Computer Science

quotes.quote: Seven electives from a designated list of courses in computer science and related disciplines . At least five of the electives must be taken in the New Brunswick Department of Computer Science (i.e., they must be 01:198:xxx), of which at least two must be at the 300 level or above.
A CS Advisor will help you make selections from this list to complete your CS major.
However, at most one of a student's electives may be one of these courses. Whether or not a given instance of 493/494 counts for elective credit depends on the individual arrangement.

requirements.notes: One complete set: a physics sequence or a chemistry sequence, as the prose lists them.

program_rules.name: Courses that earn no credit for declared CS majors
program_rules.source_prose: Declared computer science majors (198) will not receive credit (major or degree) for subsequent enrollment in computer science 105, 107,110, 142, 170, or 405.

program_rules.name: Minimum seven courses in the Rutgers-New Brunswick CS department
program_rules.not_evaluable_reason: The rule requires knowing which courses were taken AT Rutgers-New Brunswick. StudentCourse records no transfer provenance, and a cross-listed course carries another department's code, so the count cannot be computed without guessing. Rutgers publishes no transfer-equivalence rule we could apply here.
program_rules.source_prose: A minimum of seven courses must be taken in the Rutgers University-New Brunswick Department of Computer Science.

conflicts.summary: Catalog 2026-2027 requires 01:198:111 and 112; the department B.S. page requires 121 and 122 and says the new sequence begins Spring 2027. In the loaded Spring 2027 listing, 01:198:111 is not offered and 01:198:120 and 121 are. Not resolved: no official transition or equivalence policy is archived.
